title: Bank shares rise on rate hike hopes, more revenue from UPI MDR; PNB, Axis Bank lead gains- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: 15                          Quick, easy & completely paperless. So far, there is no clarity on how the rate will be split between banks, payment processors, and NPCI   September 16, 2026 / 13:52 IST             Shares of banks traded higher on September 16 on hopes of more revenue as the government approved charging a fee on person-to-merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 on Unified Payments Interface. There's also optimism around the possibility of an interest rate hike. Market participants expect the US Federal Reserve to hike benchmark rates in its monetary policy decision later in the day. If that happens, the Reserve Bank of India is expected to follow the same road, which allows banks to increase their loan prices and grow their profit margins National Payments Corp. of India Tuesday introduced a  merchant discount rate  of up to 0.4% on UPI person-to-merchant transactions exceeding Rs 2,000, which will be effective from October 15. Brokerages called the move "structurally positive", but said the earnings benefit would vary by transaction mix, exemptions and the eventual sharing of fees among stakeholders. So far, there is no clarity on how the rate will be split between banks, payment processors, and National Payments Corp. of India. Merchants pay ​the fee to banks ⁠that process the transactions with a portion also passed on to payment apps, such as Google Pay and PhonePe, that facilitate such payments. Citi estimated an annual revenue pool ​of Rs 16,000 crore to Rs 17,000 crore, with about 60% going to banks, 25% to app ​providers and 15% to aggregators. It named  Yes Bank  the standout banking beneficiary, followed by Bank of Baroda, Punjab National ‌Bank ⁠and IndusInd Bank. Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank gained 1% and 1.5%, respectively, while IndusInd Bank reversed early gains to trade 1% lower. Nearly 93% of investors now expect the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates to 3.75–4%, as per the CME FedWatch tool. The RBI is expected to raise its repo rate from 5.25% currently as inflation is seen moving higher, Systematix Institutional Equities said in a report. Shares of Nifty 50 bank constituents State Bank of India, Axis Bank, and Kotak Mahindra Bank rose nearly 2%. Yes Bank shares rose up to 4%. The Nifty Bank, Nifty PSU Bank, and Nifty Private Bank rose around 1% each. At 1:35 pm on September 16, Bank Nifty was trading 0.8% higher at 56,230.55. "Index is currently placed around the lower band of the last 11-week range 56,000-58,700. A breach and close below last week low of 55,700 levels will signal extension of the corrective decline towards 55,200 and 54,800 levels in the coming sessions. Immediate bias in the index remains down below 57,000 levels and only a formation of higher high and higher low on a sustained basis in the daily chart and a close above 57,000 levels will signal a pause in the current down trend," said Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking.
